turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, I just checked him. Blood pressure is 138 over 86, pulse is 78. My sister gets a buzzing in her ears after every diwali, her own problem, so ears always catch my eye. Please go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come, sit. What brings you today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, good morning. Umm, the bus was packed and some fellow kept talking on speaker phone, anyway that is not why. I have this ringing in my right ear.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He will go round and round. It is three weeks now. And he has giddiness, he holds the doorframe.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Err, no giddiness. I am not dizzy at all. The ringing is the right ear only, and it is since one month, not three weeks.

[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Let me say it back. Right ear ringing, somewhere between three weeks and one month, the two of you don't match. You are saying no giddiness. Is the sound there all day?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): All the time, but worse when it is quiet. In a noisy place I hardly notice. At night with the fan off it is loud, like a cicada in the wall.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Does the right ear feel muffled, or is the hearing normal?

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Muffled, like cotton in it. On the phone I miss words if I use the right side. Left side is okay. My neighbour had his ear washed, he told me a full bus story, I won't start that.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the ear?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No pain.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any discharge, pus or water?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing coming out.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever. The canteen sambhar was too spicy yesterday, that is a separate complaint, ha.
[SEG0016] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Also he is careless with the pressure tablet. Amlodipin ten mg, and he skips it two three times in a week.
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): That is wrong. I take it every morning, with water. It is five mg, the small white tablet, not ten. I have been on it for years for my BP.

[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. I will note amlodipine once each morning for the blood pressure, but I will not write a dose, five and ten are both being said. And I cannot be sure the doses are actually taken daily. Any allergy to any medicine?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No allergy. Nothing.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any ear operation, or any surgery at all?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No operations. Everything is original, doctor.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): How is the stomach, any acidity or loose stools?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Stomach is fine. No loose motion.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or take alcohol?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. Alcohol, uh, a small peg at a wedding only, not regular. Hardly.
[SEG0026] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, the old file. My child had an ear infection last monsoon, we struggled with the drops, so I get worried for everyone. I will wait outside.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Let me look in the ears. Stay still a moment.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): The right drum is intact. A little wax on the canal wall, but it is not blocking, I can see the drum. Left ear is clear, drum normal.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Wax? So you will wash it? My cousin in Pune said the washing made him dizzy for one hour, big drama.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): My first plan was olive oil drops for five days, then you come back in one week and I syringe the wax out.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Before I lock that, tell me what work you do, and if you are around loud sound.

[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh, the machine shop. I run the power press and a small generator, sometimes twelve hours, very loud. Umm, I don't wear the ear muffs, they feel hot, so I just go in. Supervisor shouts about tea, that is his hobby, not medical.
[SEG0033] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I have told him so many times. Even the cotton he used to stuff, he stopped that.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Cotton falls out only, it is useless. I stopped last year.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah, that changes my plan. The wax is not the cause, and this noise history matters more. No drops, and no syringing. I am cancelling the one week wax visit.

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): What I think is going on, and this is not a final diagnosis, the loud noise over years can tire the tiny hair cells in the inner ear, and the hearing nerve keeps firing a ring even in a quiet room. Working impression is noise-related ringing, and maybe some hearing loss on the right. We need a test before I say more.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): So the machine did it. I knew the muffs were not just for show. There was a sale at the bus stand, blue ones, I walked past, typical me.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please use proper ear muffs at the press and near the generator, every shift. Not cotton. And keep the phone volume down.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay, I will buy them this week. My wife will not let me forget, she already reminds me about milk packets.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will refer you to audiology for a hearing test, a pure tone audiogram. Consider it booked from our side, not a maybe.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And when do we see you?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in four weeks with the report. If the report is slow we still meet. The one week idea is gone.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): If the ringing gets much worse before four weeks, or I start spinning?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it suddenly becomes much louder, or you get true spinning, or the hearing drops off fast, come earlier, do not wait. Otherwise the four week visit stands.
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): At night I switch the fan on and the ring is less. Is that alright to do?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, a little background sound is fine, it masks it. Do not use earphones loud to cover the ringing.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Good. One last thing, the parking fellow outside argued about ten rupees, can you believe, in this heat.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Muffs at work, the hearing test, and I see you in four weeks. Take care.

spec.situation: Ringing in the right ear for a month, worse in quiet; works with loud machinery without ear protection; some muffled hearing; hearing test referral.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

omissions.text: Patient denied dizziness/giddiness ('no giddiness', 'not dizzy at all'). The recorded facts instead list giddiness as present/disputed without capturing the explicit negative from the patient.
Right-sided hearing difficulty detail not recorded: 'On the phone I miss words if I use the right side'; left side is okay.
Negative finding not recorded: left ear is okay/normal from the patient's history.
Medication dose detail from the patient not recorded: amlodipine 5 mg, small white tablet, taken every morning.
Negative finding not recorded: no acidity.

The planned olive oil drops for five days, return in one week, and ear syringing were explicitly cancelled after the noise exposure history; the cancellation of this initial wax-management plan and cancellation of the one-week wax visit are not recorded.
Audiology referral was framed as definite/consider it booked from our side, not merely considered.
Follow-up nuance not recorded: return in four weeks with the report, but still come in four weeks even if the report is delayed.
